observed.facings.png: Three offline scene renders at one shared scale, labelled 'after Scrapper Timber lowered rot S / E / N'. Each shows a tan ground bank, a dark rectangular pit, and a one-lane timber deck with copper plates and rope lashings spanning the pit. Two small timber-and-copper anchor posts stand on each bank, and a thin tan rope runs from each post to the deck end. S and N are tall layouts; E is a wide layout.
observed.south.png: Lowered, rot S. The deck runs north–south across a pit about three lanes wide. Two small anchors stand above the pit on the north bank and two below it on the south bank, each about 25×40 px, made of brown wood with rope lashing and copper/red fittings. A single rope runs straight from each anchor into the deck end, with no gap. The south pair is the north pair's sprite turned 180°.
observed.east.png: Lowered, rot E. The deck runs east–west across a pit that spans the full height. Two anchors sit on each bank, drawn lying horizontally with their clamps toward the deck, and a straight rope runs from each clamp to the deck end with no gap. The anchors look like the S sprite rotated 90°.
observed.north.png: Lowered, rot N. Same layout as S: ropes run continuously from the four anchors to both deck ends. The deck pattern differs slightly (plates offset), and the anchors are identical to S.
observed.scale.png: The rot E lowered render with a vanilla human standing on the east bank. The human is about 70 px wide and 110 px tall. Each anchor is about 40 px long and 20 px tall, roughly knee-sized beside the human. The deck lane is about one human wide.
observed.assembled_1.png: Lowered, rot W. Mirrors E: four horizontal anchors, two per bank, each with a straight rope reaching the deck end. No gaps.
observed.assembled_2.png: Raised, rot E. The pit lies right of centre. The raised leaf is a thin vertical brown pole with iron bands, standing at the pit's west edge and rising about 270 px. A small dark hook or curl sits at its top. Each of the four anchors has a short loose rope loop (a C-shaped arc) lying on its own bank, facing the pit but stopping before its edge. No rope crosses the pit. The west loops end close to the leaf's base.
observed.assembled_3.png: Raised, rot W. Mirror of E: the leaf pole stands at the pit's east edge, with the same small dark curl at its top. Slack C-loops lie on both banks, and none crosses the pit.
observed.assembled_4.png: Raised, rot N. The leaf is shown face-on as a tall plank door with four iron bands, standing in the pit area with an iron hinge bar at the pit's south edge. The north anchors sit above the pit with rope loops hanging down short of the pit edge. The south anchors sit below the pit with rope loops arching up short of the pit edge. No rope crosses the pit.
observed.assembled_5.png: Raised, rot S. The leaf is shown face-on as a plank door with Z-bracing and iron corner plates, rising from a hinge bar at the pit's north edge and covering the north bank where the north anchors would stand. Only the south pair of anchors is visible, with slack rope arcs short of the pit. The north anchors and their ropes cannot be seen at all, apparently hidden behind the leaf.

CAMERA.seen: The anchor sprite is rotated in the image plane with the rope direction: upright in S/N, turned 180° for the opposite bank, and lying horizontally in E/W. This is how a top-down sprite behaves when rotated, not an upright post seen from the 35° camera. The deck and leaf follow the building camera.

BORE.seen: Solid ropes only; no open bore is shown anywhere.

PORTS.seen: Lowered S/N/E/W: each rope leaves its anchor clamp and meets the deck end at the same row, with no gap on either bank. Raised: ropes are disconnected and lie as slack loops, as the rule requires.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Each visible anchor has exactly one rope fitting, pointing toward the deck it faces. No extra connectors.

LAYERS.seen: Raised S: the upright leaf at the north hinge draws over the north-bank anchors behind it, which is physically consistent. Raised N: the south anchors draw in front of the leaf hinge. Ropes draw under the anchors and over the ground.

ROTATIONS.seen: The same timber, copper and rope anchor and the same palette appear in every rotation. The two leaf faces in S and N differ (Z-brace vs banded planks), which reads as the two sides of one leaf.

SIGNATURE.seen: Lowered ropes are continuous in every rotation, and raised ropes are slack loops on the banks with nothing crossing the pit. However, in raised rot S the north anchors and their slack loops are completely hidden. A small dark hook or curl at the top of the raised leaf in E/W cannot be told apart from a rope stub.

MATERIAL.seen: The anchors read as weathered wood with rope lashing and copper/rust plates, and the rope reads as tan fibre.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Each anchor sits well inside its single cell (about 25×40 px in a roughly 96 px cell): small but not overflowing. It is a small object beside the human.

ALPHA.seen: Every image is a scene composite on a ground and pit fill (the card measures real alpha as False on all facings). The anchor texture's own cut-out cannot be inspected without a transparent render.

OURS.seen: The Scrapper Timber look matches the mod's deck tile, and no vanilla or donor art is recognisable.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the ropes (1–2 px at the render scale) shrink below one pixel, and each anchor becomes about 8×10 px. Lowered rope continuity and raised slack loops would not read at normal zoom.

Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline

request.prompt: A single RimWorld map sprite of a drawbridge anchor bollard in the Scrapper timber look, on a fully transparent background. Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, crisp cut-out edges. Camera: the standard RimWorld building view, tilted about 35 degrees from above. The bollard is an upright, stout weathered-timber post standing on the ground in a 1x1 tile: its lit flat top face is visible at the upper end, a darker front face band runs below it, and its height rises toward the top of the image. The post is drawn the same way up in every rotation, standing, never lying flat and never upside-down. A rough iron clamp band is bolted to the side of the post that faces the bridge deck, and a thick braided rope is fastened at that clamp. LOWERED state: the rope runs unbroken and taut from the clamp to the end of the deck with no gap, on both banks. RAISED state: the deck stands upright at the hinge bank as a tall leaf whose top ends in plain timber and iron hardware (flat timber cap, bolted iron band) with no rope, stub, hook or curl attached; each bollard's rope is slack and disconnected, lying as a loose coiled loop on the ground beside its bollard, with nothing crossing or pointing over the dark pit; the bollards and slack loops on both banks sit beside or clear of the upright leaf so they stay fully visible. Deck squares are the plain deck tile for context and the pit is a flat dark rectangle. Muted browns and weathered grey wood, dark iron, tan rope. reference: none.

The bollards are the same sprite turned 90° to lie sideways, clamps facing the deck: the west pair points east and the east pair points west. Straight ropes reach the deck edges at x≈192 and x≈478. The upper rope in each pair is a lighter grey than the lower one.

observed.assembled_2.png: Raised, rotation E. The deck is gone from the pit. A tall, thin grey steel bar (the leaf seen edge-on) stands on the west pit edge and extends up/north to about y=155. Each of the four bollards has a short J-shaped slack rope curling on its own bank. The west pair's loops end just short of the leaf base, the east pair's loops are on the east bank, and no rope crosses the pit.
observed.assembled_3.png: Raised, rotation W. A mirror of E: the leaf bar stands on the east pit edge. The same J-shaped slack loops sit on both banks, and nothing crosses the pit or rises from the top of the leaf.
observed.assembled_4.png: Raised, rotation N. The hinge is on the south pit edge and the riveted steel leaf is drawn upward over the pit. The north-bank bollards have J-loops hanging down toward the pit, ending about 20 px short of the pit edge. The south-bank bollards have J-loops arcing upward toward the hinge. observed.assembled_5.png: Raised, rotation S. The hinge is on the north pit edge and a braced steel leaf is drawn upward over the north bank (y≈195–478). CAMERA.seen: The bollard is a single top-down clamp sprite that is rotated per placement: flipped 180° for the south bank and turned 90° for east/west, where it lies sideways. BORE.seen: There are no pipes or hoses, only solid ropes. No open bore is drawn anywhere.

PORTS.seen: Lowered S/N/E/W: each rope starts at its bollard's clamp jaw and ends at the deck edge with no visible gap. Raised: the ropes leave the clamp and lie slack on the bank.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Each bollard has one rope leaving its clamp toward the deck it faces. There are no extra connectors.

LAYERS.seen: Raised S: the upright leaf fully covers the north-bank bollards and their ropes. This is physically plausible (they sit behind a standing leaf), but it hides both bollards, so I cannot tell whether the order is intended.

ROTATIONS.seen: The same sprite, palette and rope colour appear in every rotation. Only the in-plane rotation differs, which is covered under CAMERA. The rope shades differ slightly (lighter upper rope in E/W).

SIGNATURE.seen: Lowered: continuous ropes on both banks in all four rotations. Raised E/W/N: slack J-loops on both banks, nothing over the pit, nothing rising from the leaf top. Raised S: the hinge-bank bollards and their slack loops are not visible, so 'on both banks, in every rotation' cannot be confirmed.

MATERIAL.seen: Rusted steel plate with a grey metal jaw and visible rivets reads as weathered metal, in the Scrapper look.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Each bollard sits well inside one cell: roughly 25×35 px against a cell about the pawn's width. It neither overflows nor looks lost.

ALPHA.seen: These are composed scene renders on an opaque ground (the card measures real alpha False for every facing), so the bollard's own cut-out cannot be judged here. No halo is visible around the bollards against the ground.

OURS.seen: Own Scrapper-family clamp art matching the deck's rust palette. No vanilla or donor sprite is recognisable.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the bollard is about 12–17 px: a dark-outlined rust block with a 1 px line leaving it. It still reads as an anchor post with a rope, though the rope is near the limit.

reply.image_seen: Image 1 combines three lowered bridge orientations; image 2 shows a vertical deck with four end anchors; image 3 shows a horizontal deck with four sideways anchors; image 4 shows the opposite vertical orientation; image 5 adds a human beside the horizontal bridge; image 6 shows the opposite horizontal lowered orientation; images 7 and 8 show thin upright leaves on opposite banks with four anchors and loose cable loops, against tan banks and dark rectangular pits.

concerns.evidence: In south.png and north.png, the lower anchors invert the upper anchors' broad cap and tapered clamp arrangement. In east.png and assembled_1.png, that same arrangement turns sideways with the cable. The entire bollard silhouette rotates in the image plane instead of retaining an upright post with a consistently visible top.

The referenced assembled_5.png, raised south view, is absent. The supplied raised east and west views show all four anchors and their bank loops, but cannot establish visibility behind a south-facing raised leaf.

The supplied raised east and west leaves occupy narrow strips beside the pit, with the anchors and loops alongside them. Neither shows the reported south-facing overlap. A raised south capture is needed to determine whether the leaf correctly occludes the anchors.

In east.png and assembled_1.png, the upper straight cable has a visibly pale grey center while the lower straight cable reads darker brown. The paired vertical cables in south.png and north.png have more closely matching tones. The difference is visible, although lighting could explain it.
